answer: When a small quake occurs, its P-wave reaches nearby stations seconds apart, so a claimant reports the arrival second it felt, and regional stations must confirm the same wave with consistent travel times. The arrival order is fixed by geology, not by choice, and no oasis of calm data can hide a missing arrival; a mesa of fake reports fails because one recording gives only one arrival time, and a sparrow light single report is not enough without neighbours confirming the same wave.
